---
title: "A Poisson-regression analysis"
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

The Nettle language-rate model makes the log-base requirement visible: the primary fit uses natural-log area as a fixed exposure offset, while the diagnostic inserts the source's base-10 column directly. <!-- dqr-allow: reference-metadata --> Because the upstream course repository states no license, the fallback below downloads and verifies the exact source.

```{r}
#| label: load-nettle-application
#| echo: true
path <- "data/nettle/nettle-1999-climate.csv"
if (file.exists(path)) {
  nettle <- read.csv(path)
} else {
  url <- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bodowinter/",
                "applied_statistics_book_data/master/nettle_1999_climate.csv")
  source_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  download.file(url, source_file, mode = "wb")
  stopifnot(digest::digest(source_file, "sha256", file = TRUE, serialize = FALSE) ==
    "3c5abfbec7b2132a9b81ee9a178cbd5559426578032b60c6c4ad74046898793b")
  raw <- read.csv(source_file)
  nettle <- data.frame(country = raw$Country, log10_population = raw$Population,
    log10_area_km2 = raw$Area, log_area_km2 = log(10) * raw$Area,
    mean_growing_season_months = raw$MGS, language_count = as.integer(raw$Langs))
}
correct <- glm(language_count ~ mean_growing_season_months + offset(log_area_km2),
               poisson(), nettle)
mismatched <- glm(language_count ~ mean_growing_season_months + offset(log10_area_km2),
                  poisson(), nettle)
data.frame(
  offset = c("natural log area", "base-10 log area inserted directly"),
  mgs_coefficient = c(coef(correct)[[2L]], coef(mismatched)[[2L]]),
  rate_ratio = exp(c(coef(correct)[[2L]], coef(mismatched)[[2L]]))
)
```

The mismatch changes the coefficient because it no longer encodes $\lambda_i=A_i r_i$ with an exposure coefficient of one.

```{r}
#| label: nettle-application-plot
#| echo: true
library(ggplot2)
nettle$observed_rate <- nettle$language_count / exp(nettle$log_area_km2)
grid <- data.frame(mean_growing_season_months =
  seq(min(nettle$mean_growing_season_months),
      max(nettle$mean_growing_season_months), length.out = 200L))
grid$fitted_rate <- exp(coef(correct)[[1L]] + coef(correct)[[2L]] *
                          grid$mean_growing_season_months)
ggplot(nettle, aes(mean_growing_season_months, observed_rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  geom_line(data = grid, aes(y = fitted_rate), color = "#1F5A85", linewidth = .8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Mean growing season (months)", y = "Languages per square kilometer") +
  theme_classic()
```

The fitted positive association answers a conditional, descriptive question under a fixed-area-exposure assumption. Countries are not experimental units assigned to climates; area is not literally observation time; and Nettle's original specification estimated its coefficient. None of these fits supports a causal ecological claim.
